questions.question: Blood Relations: His father is the only son of my father-in-law. How are they related?
questions.hint: Only son of father-in-law is husband. Husband's son is her son.

questions.question: Blood Relations: She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather. How are they related?
questions.hint: Only son of grandfather is father. Father's daughter is sister.

questions.question: Blood Relations: A + B means A is father of B; A - B means A is sister of B; A * B means A is son of B. What does P + Q - R * S imply?. How are they related?
questions.hint: P is father of Q & R, S is mother of R => P & S married.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Pointing to a man, a woman said: 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.'. How are they related?
questions.hint: Only daughter of mother is self. She is his mother.

questions.question: Blood Relations: X is brother of Y. Y is wife of Z. Z is son of W. How is X related to Z?. How are they related?
questions.hint: X is wife's brother => Brother-in-law.

questions.question: Blood Relations: If P is father of Q, R is son of S, T is brother of P, and Q is sister of R, how is S related to T?. How are they related?
questions.hint: S is mother of Q & R (P's wife). T is P's brother => Sister-in-law.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Introducing a boy, a girl said, 'He is the son of the daughter of the father of my uncle.'. How are they related?
questions.hint: Father of uncle is grandfather. Grandfather's daughter is aunt/mother. Her son is cousin.

questions.question: Blood Relations: A's mother is sister of B and daughter of C. D is daughter of B and sister of E. How is C related to E?. How are they related?
questions.hint: C is parent of B, B is parent of E => C is grandparent.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Showing a picture of an old man, Amit said, 'His son is my son's uncle.' How is the old man related to Amit?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Amit's son's uncle is Amit's brother. Old man is his father.

questions.question: Blood Relations: M is sister of N. N is father of O. P is wife of M. How is O related to M?. How are they related?
questions.hint: M is aunt of O.

questions.question: Blood Relations: A is father of B, but B is not his son. How is B related to A?. How are they related?
questions.hint: B is A's daughter.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Pointing to a photograph, Rakesh said, 'She is the mother of my son's wife.' How is Rakesh related to the woman?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Son's wife is daughter-in-law. Her mother is co-in-law.

questions.question: Blood Relations: If A is B's sister, C is B's mother, D is C's father, E is D's mother, how is A related to D?. How are they related?
questions.hint: D is C's father, C is A's mother => A is granddaughter.

questions.question: Blood Relations: B is the brother of A, whose mother is C. D is the father of C. How is B related to D?. How are they related?
questions.hint: C is mother of B, D is father of C => B is grandson.

questions.question: Blood Relations: E is brother of B, A is sister of B. How is A related to E?. How are they related?
questions.hint: A and E are siblings.

questions.question: Blood Relations: K is brother of T. T is wife of M. M is son of R. How is K related to R?. How are they related?
questions.hint: K is brother of R's daughter-in-law.

questions.question: Blood Relations: P is brother of Q. R is mother of Q. S is father of R. T is mother of S. How is P related to S?. How are they related?
questions.hint: R is mother of P, S is father of R => P is grandson.

questions.question: Blood Relations: A and B are married couple. X and Y are brothers. X is brother of A. How is Y related to B?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Y is A's brother => B's brother-in-law.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Rahul told Anand, 'Yesterday I defeated the only brother of the daughter of my grandmother.' Who did Rahul defeat?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Daughter of grandmother is aunt. Her only brother is father.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Deepak has a brother Anil. Deepak is the son of Prem. Vimal is Prem's father. In terms of relationship, how is Anil related to Vimal?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Prem is father of Anil, Vimal is father of Prem => Anil is grandson.

questions.question: Blood Relations: If 'A $ B' means A is father of B, 'A # B' means A is mother of B, what does P $ Q # R mean?. How are they related?
options: P is maternal grandfather of R
questions.hint: P is father of Q, Q is mother of R => P is maternal grandfather.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Looking at a portrait, a man said, 'I have no brother or sister, but that man's father is my father's son.' Whose portrait is it?. How are they related?
questions.hint: Father's son is himself. 'That man's father is me' => His son.

questions.question: Blood Relations: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. F is A's son. How is F related to D?. How are they related?
questions.hint: D is grandfather of A. F is son of A => Great-grandson.

questions.question: Blood Relations: M is father of N, L is brother of M, P is mother of L. How is N related to P?. How are they related?
questions.hint: P is mother of M, N is child of M => Grandchild.

questions.question: Blood Relations: Q is mother of P. P is wife of R. S is brother of R. How is S related to Q?. How are they related?
questions.hint: P is Q's daughter. R is P's husband. S is R's brother.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All cars are trucks. All trucks are vehicles.. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: Both Conclusion I and II follow
questions.hint: Conclusion I: All cars are vehicles. Conclusion II: Some vehicles are trucks.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some pens are books. All books are pencils.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Intersection of pens and books falls inside pencils.

questions.question: Syllogisms: No cat is dog. All dogs are lions.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Dogs are inside lions and outside cats.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sweet.. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows conclusively
questions.hint: No direct link between apples and sweet.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Only a few doors are windows. All windows are walls.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: 'Only a few' implies both some are and some are not.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some doctors are engineers. All engineers are scientists. No scientist is pilot.. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: No doctor is pilot is a possibility
questions.hint: No engineer is pilot, but doctors can overlap.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Statements: All A are B. No B is C. All C are D.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: C ⊂ D and C ∩ B = Ø.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Statements: Some red are blue. Some blue are green. Some green are yellow.. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: None of the universal conclusions follow
questions.hint: Chain of 'Some' yields no universal relation.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Statements: All rain is water. No water is fire. Some fire is smoke.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Smoke that is fire cannot be water.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Statements: Only a few books are papers. No paper is pen.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Books that are papers cannot be pens.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All shirts are pants. All pants are shoes.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Transitive relation.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some birds are insects. All insects are butterflies.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Overlap extends to butterflies.

questions.question: Syllogisms: No river is ocean. All oceans are seas.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Oceans are inside seas and outside rivers.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Classic Aristotelian syllogism.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some stars are planets. No planet is moon.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Stars that are planets cannot be moons.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Only a few mobile are laptop. All laptop are computer.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: 'Only a few' guarantees intersection.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All metals are solids. All solids are hard.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Transitive.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some teachers are scholars. Some scholars are authors.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Two 'Some' statements yield no universal link.

questions.question: Syllogisms: No student is lazy. All lazy are failing.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Lazy individuals are outside students.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All trees are plants. No plant is animal.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Trees are inside plants, plants disjoint from animals.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some dogs are friendly. All friendly creatures are loyal.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Overlap.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Only a few chairs are tables. No table is desk.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Chairs that are tables cannot be desks.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All fruits are healthy. All healthy foods are organic.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Transitive.

questions.question: Syllogisms: Some books are novels. No novel is comic.. Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.hint: Books that are novels cannot be comics.

questions.question: Syllogisms: All rivers are water bodies. All water bodies contain water.. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: Some rivers do not contain water
questions.hint: Transitive.

questions.question: Reasoning Puzzle #1: In a seating alignment of 26 candidates facing North, Priya is ranked 6th from left. Simultaneously, a runner travels 5 km North, turns East 4 km, then South 5 km. What is Priya's rank from right and runner's net displacement?
